submitter: bugs_open/477 lane, opened 2026-09-04. The bug was filed by the site_delivery_and_editor lane on 2026-09-03; I asked their live session before taking it and they confirmed it is unclaimed and endorsed this order of work.
rationale:
STEP A OF THREE, and deliberately the smallest one: delete a false sentence from a customer-facing page. Nothing is added.

THE DEFECT. Both confirm pages end on "You will not get any more reminders about it." Nothing in the estate sends a reminder. Re-measured 2026-09-04 11:43Z, not carried from the bug file: exactly ONE agent can send mail (`SELECT type FROM agent_definitions WHERE default_config::text LIKE '%send_delivery_email%' AND is_active AND NOT COALESCE(is_snapshot,false) AND deleted_at IS NULL` -> delivery-email-sender); ZERO scheduled tasks target it (`SELECT count(*) FROM scheduled_tasks WHERE target_agent_type='delivery-email-sender'` -> 0, of 107 rows); and `sites.transfer_confirmed_at`, the record this button writes, has NO reader outside the file that writes it (`grep -rn "transfer_confirmed_at|TransferConfirmed" --include=*.go .` -> 6 hits, all platform/delivery/handover.go, zero in tests). So the page asks a customer to take an action, tells them what the action prevents, and the thing it prevents does not exist and is not recorded anywhere anything reads.

WHY DELETE RATHER THAN REWORD. The button's stated MOTIVATION was the false part. Any replacement motivation I invent ("so we know not to chase you", "this closes the file at our end") is a fresh claim about a mechanism, which is the same defect one wording along - and this is the third instance of that exact class today (bugs_open/475: the email says the ZIP contains instructions, it contains none; bugs_open/476: the instructions say a local double-click works, it does not). What remains is exactly what pressing does: it tells us, and nothing is recorded until you press.

WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING. This does not fix the bug. It makes the page stop lying while the follow-up sender is built (step B), after which the wording SHOULD come back because it will be true. The tripwire test is what makes that restoration deliberate rather than accidental, and I have written its own limits into it: it matches this promise's vocabulary only, so a rewording would pass it. It is a tripwire, not a detector for the class.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE BUG FILE'S FIX CANDIDATES, both found by reading the code the candidates rest on, both relevant to what this change costs.
(1) The bug file offers this step as "One migration, no new machinery". It is NOT a migration: this copy is hardcoded Go string literals in renderConfirm (internal/core-manager/handlers/delivery.go:405-432). There is no DB row and no config key, so it needs an image and a core-manager roll, and `make release` is the owner's. It is therefore INERT on commit, exactly like bugs_open/466.
(2) Relevant to step B and stated here so the reviewers can hold me to it later: the bug file says a follow-up sender is "mostly seeding rather than Go" because the mail action already exists. It is not. SendDeliveryEmailAction calls delivery.Claim (send_delivery_email_action.go:156), which calls StampHandover, which claims the row `WHERE handed_over_at IS NULL` and returns ErrAlreadyDelivered for any site already handed over (platform/delivery/prepare.go:261-267). Every site a follow-up targets is by definition already handed over, so the existing action refuses by design exactly the population the follow-up exists for. Step B needs its own action. Nothing in THIS submission depends on that; it is disclosed because it changes the shape of the work these reviewers will see next.

OWNER STATE, so no seat mistakes this for an executed instruction. The owner has NOT ruled. His words were "maybe repeat them in the first follow up email that would normally go a week or so later" - a suggestion in passing, which is what prompted the bug. The interval, the recipient rule, and the fact that the first working test WILL email him (idea.uk is the only selectable row and its delivery address is his) are all open, and all held for him at step B. They do not gate this deletion.

CONSUMERS TOLD. The only other lane touching this surface is site_delivery_and_editor (bugs_open/475's copy work). They verified at file level that 475's surface is platform/delivery/prepare.go, the placeholder vocabulary in send_delivery_email_action.go:125-132, and a migration for the email body_template - no overlap with renderConfirm - and have recorded in their handoff that they stay out of delivery.go and handover.go.

plan.summary: Delete the sentence "You will not get any more reminders about it." from both confirm-page outcomes (the GET button page and the POST success page), replacing it with nothing. Record WHY in a comment at the site, naming what would make it true again. Add one test that fails if the promise returns, so restoring it is a deliberate act rather than a copy-paste.

edits.rationale: The page a customer lands on from the emailed link. Same deletion. The existing comment (no em dashes, nothing named, say that nothing has happened yet) is kept and extended with the measured reason for the deletion and the exact condition for restoring it, so the next reader does not re-add it as an improvement.

A tripwire, and its comment says it is meant to be deleted one day. It serves BOTH pages through the real router (the fake confirms any token, so the POST renders the true success page, not a failure page) and fails if either mentions a reminder. PROVEN BY MUTATION, both arms separately: restoring the sentence on the button page alone fails it; restoring it on the success page alone fails it; the restored file is green at -count=1. Its limits are written into the test rather than left implied - it matches this promise's vocabulary only, so "we will not chase you" would pass, and it cannot check that no sender exists. The class of defect (customer-facing copy promising a mechanism the code lacks) has no automated detector in the estate, and this test does not claim to be one.
